en: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a wingspan of up to two meters, making it larger than most other eagles.
The original Philippine flag features eight rays on the sun, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish rule in 1896.
The Philippine Senate has exactly 24 elected senators, which is much smaller than the House of Representatives that has over 300 members.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English are the only two officially used in national government and schools.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu attracts over two million attendees annually, making it one of the largest and most famous Philippine festivals.
The Lumad people comprise about 18 distinct indigenous ethnolinguistic groups living mainly in the Mindanao region of the southern Philippines.
Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed, but he had already written two famous novels and studied in eight countries.
The Philippines is home to over 1,100 orchid species, including the rare Vanda sanderiana, which is known as the Queen of Philippine orchids.
Filipino citizens can vote in national elections once they reach 18 years of age, provided they have lived in the Philippines for at least one year.
Filipino scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo built a bamboo incubator in 1957 that cost 90 percent less than standard electric incubators for rural hospitals.
The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of 7,641 islands, which is over 500 more islands than the previously believed official count of 7,107.
The Philippines is divided into exactly 42,036 barangays, which are the smallest and most numerous local government units in the entire country.
